games.title: Reading Detective
games.description: Use unit evidence to solve each reading clue.

rounds.prompt: The passage says "Money is a tool." What does this mean?
choices: It means that money is not good or bad by itself; what matters is how a person chooses to use it.
He saves most of his pocket money in a tin under his bed instead of spending it all at once.
Even though she whispered that she did not belong, something small but substantial inside her told her to speak, so she wrote her name in shaky handwriting.
rounds.answer: It means that money is not good or bad by itself; what matters is how a person chooses to use it.
rounds.explanation: The passage says money is not good or bad on its own; what matters is how we use it. So calling money a tool means the person using it decides whether it does good.

rounds.prompt: In the conversation, what does Sami do with his pocket money instead of spending it all?
choices: She told him to teach himself to wait, and to buy something only if he still wanted it after three days.
She said that kindness should be a rule and not a suggestion, and that some rules feel unavoidable but are still unconstitutional because they go against fairness.
He saves most of his pocket money in a tin under his bed instead of spending it all at once.
rounds.answer: He saves most of his pocket money in a tin under his bed instead of spending it all at once.
rounds.explanation: Sami tells Maya he gets a small amount each week but does not spend it all; he says, 'I save most of it in a tin under my bed.'

rounds.prompt: Why did Amal decide to write her name on the notice board, even though she felt she did not belong?
choices: It means that money is not good or bad by itself; what matters is how a person chooses to use it.
Even though she whispered that she did not belong, something small but substantial inside her told her to speak, so she wrote her name in shaky handwriting.
She told him to teach himself to wait, and to buy something only if he still wanted it after three days.
rounds.answer: Even though she whispered that she did not belong, something small but substantial inside her told her to speak, so she wrote her name in shaky handwriting.
rounds.explanation: Amal whispered 'I don't belong', but the story says something inside her, small but substantial, told her to speak, so she wrote her name in shaky handwriting anyway.
